significance: One of the eight great Buddhist pilgrimage places, revered as the spot where the Buddha returned to earth after teaching the Abhidhamma to his mother in the Tushita heaven. Ashoka set up a pillar with an elephant capital, a stupa and a temple here in the third century BCE, and the ruins of Buddhist monasteries and later Hindu monuments were surveyed by Alexander Cunningham in 1842.
story: The texts say Indra built three ladders down from Mount Meru so that the Buddha and his retinue could descend to earth at Sankissa on the Mahapavarana festival day.
